name: Engine Generator 1
function: Three-phase engine-driven AC source for the No. 1 generator bus.
flow: Engine/CSD → Generator 1 → GEN 1 breaker → generator bus 1.
relationships: Controlled and protected by the generator control unit and interlocked with transfer/APU/external sources.

name: Engine Generator 2
function: Three-phase engine-driven AC source for the No. 2 generator bus.
flow: Engine/CSD → Generator 2 → GEN 2 breaker → generator bus 2.
relationships: Controlled and protected by the generator control unit and interlocked with transfer/APU/external sources.

name: APU Generator
function: Single APU-driven AC source connected to the tie bus and selected load buses through the APU/BTB controls.
flow: APU → APU generator → APU GB → tie bus → BTB 1/2.
relationships: Cannot parallel with external power or an engine-generator source on the same bus; controlled by APU GCU.

name: Generator 1 Breaker
function: Connects Generator 1 to its generator/load distribution when source and protection conditions are valid.
flow: GEN 1 → generator breaker → bus distribution.
relationships: Interlocked with generator control and bus-transfer logic.

name: Generator 2 Breaker
function: Connects Generator 2 to its generator/load distribution when source and protection conditions are valid.
flow: GEN 2 → generator breaker → bus distribution.
relationships: Interlocked with generator control and bus-transfer logic.

name: Bus Tie Breaker 1
function: Connects the No. 1 load side to alternate AC sources when permitted by transfer logic.
flow: Alternate source → BTB 1 → transfer/load bus 1.
relationships: Source-transfer interlocks prevent impermissible paralleling.

name: Bus Tie Breaker 2
function: Connects the No. 2 load side to alternate AC sources when permitted by transfer logic.
flow: Alternate source → BTB 2 → transfer/load bus 2.
relationships: Source-transfer interlocks prevent impermissible paralleling.

name: Transformer Rectifier 1
function: Converts aircraft AC power to DC Bus 1 power.
flow: AC source → TR1 → DC Bus 1.
relationships: Protected by TR 1 input and output circuitry.

name: Transformer Rectifier 2
function: Converts aircraft AC power to DC Bus 2 power.
flow: AC source → TR2 → DC Bus 2.
relationships: Protected by TR 2 input and output circuitry.

name: Transformer Rectifier 3
function: Provides the backup DC conversion path from an available main AC source.
flow: Available main AC source → TR3 → DC backup/tie path.
relationships: Provides backup to the DC system when primary TR sources are unavailable and the AC source is healthy.

name: Static Inverter
function: Converts battery DC to standby AC power following normal-source loss in AUTO/BAT standby operation.
flow: Battery bus → static inverter → standby AC bus.
relationships: Controlled by standby power transfer relays.

name: Battery Charger
function: Maintains aircraft battery charge when an approved charging source is available.
flow: AC charging source → charger → battery.
relationships: Separate from the battery discharge path and standby inverter.

name: External Power Contactor
function: Connects the external ground power source to aircraft AC distribution when interlocks permit.
flow: GPU receptacle → external power contactor → AC distribution.
relationships: Interlocked against impermissible source paralleling.

name: Landing Gear Electrical Module
function: Contains control/safety relays and solid-state circuits for landing gear control and indication.
flow: Proximity sensors → module logic → safety relays / indications.
relationships: Works with air/ground sensing and gear-position proximity sensors.

name: Landing Gear Proximity Sensors
function: Sense gear actuator proximity/position for control and indication.
flow: Gear actuator target → proximity sensor → landing gear electrical module.
relationships: Provides downlock/uplock/transit and safety-sensing inputs.

name: Air/Ground Safety Sensors
function: Provide the air/ground safety signals that gate landing gear selector operation.
flow: Air/ground sensor → safety relay/module → gear selector lock logic.
relationships: Ground sensing prevents normal UP selection on the ground; maintenance test circuits can isolate/verify the safety relays.

name: Left Inboard Brake
function: Left main-wheel inboard brake supplied by the System A brake path.
flow: Brake metering → brake unit → wheel.
relationships: Antiskid channel modulates the applied pressure.

name: Right Inboard Brake
function: Right main-wheel inboard brake supplied by the System A brake path.
flow: Brake metering → brake unit → wheel.
relationships: Antiskid channel modulates the applied pressure.

name: Left Outboard Brake
function: Left main-wheel outboard brake supplied by the System B brake path.
flow: Brake metering → brake unit → wheel.
relationships: Antiskid channel modulates the applied pressure.

name: Right Outboard Brake
function: Right main-wheel outboard brake supplied by the System B brake path.
flow: Brake metering → brake unit → wheel.
relationships: Antiskid channel modulates the applied pressure.

name: Left Wing Fuel Tank
function: Stores usable aircraft fuel and supplies the fuel feed manifold.
flow: Tank → boost pump / suction feed → engine manifold.
relationships: Feeds engine 1 directly and either engine through crossfeed/manifold paths as configured.

name: Center Fuel Tank
function: Center-tank fuel source for the main fuel feed system.
flow: Center tank → boost pump → fuel manifold.
relationships: Feeds the engine fuel manifold through electrically powered boost pumps and associated check/manifold valves.

name: Right Wing Fuel Tank
function: Stores usable aircraft fuel and supplies the fuel feed manifold.
flow: Tank → boost pump / suction feed → engine manifold.
relationships: Feeds engine 2 directly and either engine through crossfeed/manifold paths as configured.

name: Fuel Boost Pump Set
function: Electrically driven boost pumps provide positive fuel pressure to the engine feed manifold.
flow: Tank → boost pump → check valve → manifold.
relationships: 115-V three-phase electrical loads; pumps in a tank are arranged on separate buses so loss of one bus does not remove every pump in that tank.

name: Fuel Crossfeed Valve
function: Connects the left and right engine fuel manifolds for crossfeed operation.
flow: Left manifold ↔ crossfeed valve ↔ right manifold.
relationships: 28V DC motor-operated valve; controlled by the fuel system switching logic.

name: Engine 1 Fuel Shutoff Valve
function: Shuts fuel flow to engine 1.
flow: Fuel manifold → shutoff valve → engine 1 fuel control.
relationships: 28V DC motor-operated valve; coordinated with engine/fire control functions.

name: Engine 2 Fuel Shutoff Valve
function: Shuts fuel flow to engine 2.
flow: Fuel manifold → shutoff valve → engine 2 fuel control.
relationships: 28V DC motor-operated valve; coordinated with engine/fire control functions.

name: APU Fuel Valve
function: Controls fuel supply to the APU fuel control.
flow: Aircraft fuel source → APU fuel valve → APU fuel control.
relationships: APU start and shutdown sequence; fire control can close fuel supply.

name: Fuel Quantity Indicating System
function: Measures and displays fuel quantity for the aircraft tanks.
flow: Tank units / compensators → indicating system → cockpit displays.
relationships: Requires electrical power; testable from the indicating system.

name: Fire Protection System Module P8-1
function: Monitors fire/overheat detection and controls engine/APU fire extinguishing functions.
flow: Detector loops → warning/control module → crew indications and extinguisher control.
relationships: Contains engine/APU warning lights, overheat indications, detector test, bell cutout and extinguisher controls.
controls: Fire test / bell cutout / fire switches

name: Engine 1 Fire/Overheat Detection
function: Detects engine 1 fire and overheat conditions.
flow: Detector loop → fire protection module.
relationships: Feeds engine 1 fire warning and extinguishing control logic.

name: Engine 2 Fire/Overheat Detection
function: Detects engine 2 fire and overheat conditions.
flow: Detector loop → fire protection module.
relationships: Feeds engine 2 fire warning and extinguishing control logic.

name: Main Wheel-Well Overheat Detection
function: Detects wheel-well overheat/fire conditions.
flow: Detector → fire protection module → warning.
relationships: Provides wheel-well overheat warning and master caution path.

name: Engine Fire Extinguisher Bottles
function: Two fixed extinguisher bottles provide two-shot capability to either engine.
flow: Bottle → manifold/tubing → selected engine nozzles.
relationships: Selected through the engine fire switch/fire handle and bottle discharge circuits.

name: Cargo Smoke Detection / CEU Set
function: Effectivity-dependent forward/aft lower cargo smoke detection with detector loops and CEUs.
flow: Detector A/B → CEU → fire warning/control.
relationships: Installed on 737-200 passenger airplanes incorporating SB 26A1081.

name: Cargo Fire Extinguishing Bottle
function: Effectivity-dependent cargo fire extinguishing bottle and distribution plumbing.
flow: Bottle → discharge tubing → forward/aft cargo nozzles.
relationships: Effectivity-dependent on SB 26A1081.

name: APU Air Inlet Door Actuator
function: Electrically-driven actuator that opens and closes the APU air inlet door, admitting compressor inlet air and accessory cooling air.
flow: Fuel valve opens first; once fully open, power transfers to this actuator (~17–20 s). A door position switch releases the starter lockout relay.
relationships: Sequenced with the APU fuel shutoff valve. Fire control handle commands this door closed.
controls: APU MASTER on P5. APU CONT CB on P6. No dedicated light — a slow door shows up as a failed start.

name: APU Fuel Heater
function: Warms APU fuel before the fuel control unit to prevent icing.
flow: In the supply line upstream of the FCU. A pneumatically-actuated heater control valve opens as needed.
relationships: Heat from APU compressor bleed or oil — not the main engines. Valve failed open can cycle the load control valve.
controls: None — automatic, no cockpit switch or light.

name: APU Bleed Air Valve
function: Motor-driven valve metering APU compressor discharge into the aircraft pneumatic manifold.
flow: Armed at 95% rpm. Opens in 12–14 s when APU BLEED is OPEN to avoid speed droop. Held by the differential pressure regulator and EGT thermostat.
relationships: Feeds the same manifold as engine bleed. Interlocked with APU GEN OFF BUS at 95%. DUAL BLEED protects against APU + engine bleed.
controls: APU BLEED OPEN/CLOSE on P5. DUAL BLEED light. Duct pressure and APU EGT gauges.

name: APU Fire Extinguisher Bottle
function: Stores fire-suppressant for manual discharge into the APU compartment.
flow: Armed when either FIRE SWITCH is pulled (cabin or MLG wheel well). Pull also shuts the APU down. Discharge is a separate action.
relationships: Parallel to, but separate from, engine bottles. Detection lights FIRE WARN; the switch closes fuel, bleed, inlet door, and trips the generator.
controls: FIRE SWITCH arms; discharge button fires. FIRE PROTECTION CBs on P6.

name: Pneumatic Starter
function: Turbine air motor converting manifold air into torque to accelerate N2 to self-sustaining speed.
flow: Manifold → starter valve → starter turbine → accessory gearbox → N2. Cuts out at 35–40% N2.
relationships: Shares the accessory gearbox with CSD/generator and tachometer. Air from APU, opposite engine, or ground cart.
controls: ENGINE START switch. Indicated by START VALVE OPEN and rising N2.

name: Starter Valve
function: Pneumatically-operated, solenoid-controlled butterfly metering air to the starter.
flow: In the duct between manifold and starter; opens when the start switch energizes it.
relationships: Shares the pneumatic manifold with packs and APU bleed. Remaining illuminated after cutout requires immediate shutdown.
controls: ENGINE START GRD/OFF/CONT/FLT. ENGINE START VALVES CB P6-2. START VALVE OPEN light.

name: Igniter Plugs
function: High-energy plugs in chambers 4 and 7 that ignite the fuel-air mixture.
flow: Fired by the ignition exciter in sequence with fuel introduction at IDLE.
relationships: Dependent on the exciter; both plugs fire in GRD/FLT, individual plugs in L IGN / R IGN.
controls: ENGINE START switch. START IGNITION (28V) and LOW ENERGY IGNITION (115V) CBs on P6-2.

name: Ignition Exciter
function: Capacitor-discharge unit converting 28V DC / 115V AC into high-voltage pulses.
flow: Aircraft power → exciter → high-tension leads → igniters.
relationships: Upstream of the igniters; enabled by the start switch.

name: Engine Driven AC Generator
function: Primary 115/200V 400 Hz three-phase power for the transfer buses.
flow: Driven off the accessory gearbox via CSD at constant 6000 rpm.
relationships: Paired with the CSD. Cooled by fan air. Primary in-flight electrical source.
controls: GEN 1 / GEN 2 on P5. GEN OFF BUS, BUS OFF, TRANSFER BUS OFF lights.

name: Generator Constant Speed Drive
function: Hydromechanical transmission holding generator speed at 6000 rpm across N2 range.
flow: Engine pad → CSD differential → constant 6000 rpm → generator.
relationships: Self-contained oil system with air-oil cooler. Electrically disconnectable, ground-reset only.
controls: Guarded CSD DISCONNECT. CSD LOW OIL PRESSURE / HIGH OIL TEMP lights.

name: Engine Tachometer Generator
function: Self-generating magneto providing an AC signal proportional to N1 or N2.
flow: Accessory gearbox → tach generator → N1/N2 indicators. No bus power required.
relationships: Critical during start — N2 is the crew’s cue for fuel introduction and starter cutout.
controls: Indicator lighting via AC bus (P6 indicator group).

name: Fuel Flow Transmitter
function: Measures fuel mass flow between the FCU and engine manifold.
flow: Sensing element in the fuel line → cockpit fuel flow gauge.
relationships: Read with N1 and EGT for engine performance.
controls: Engine INDICATOR group CB on P6.

name: Fuel & Oil Cooler
function: Uses engine fuel to cool lubricating oil while preheating fuel.
flow: Hot oil through tubes, cold fuel through the shell toward the FCU.
relationships: Ties oil and fuel temperature together.
controls: Oil temperature gauge and low oil pressure warning.

name: Engine Nose Dome
function: Inlet cone directing airflow into the compressor, with 8th-stage anti-ice.
flow: 8th-stage bleed → internal ducting → anti-ice exhaust. Houses the Pt2 probe.
relationships: Rotates with N1. Pt2 feeds engine indicating.
controls: ENG ANTI-ICE on P5. ANTI-ICE VALVE OPEN light.

name: 8th-Stage Engine Bleed Port
function: Primary compressor bleed source for engine pneumatic supply.
flow: 8th-stage compressor bleed port → engine bleed ducting / precooler / bleed control.
relationships: Engine compressor source; not an accessory-gearbox component.
controls: Controlled by engine bleed / pressure-ratio logic.

name: 13th-Stage Engine Bleed Port
function: High-stage compressor bleed source used when higher pressure is required.
flow: 13th-stage compressor bleed port → high-stage modulation / bleed control → engine pneumatic ducting.
relationships: Separate compressor-stage source; do not place it under the accessory gearbox.

name: Engine Bleed Air Valve
function: DC motor-driven shutoff admitting engine bleed into the pneumatic manifold.
flow: Downstream of the precooler → bleed valve → cross-feed manifold. Auto-closes at 490°F.
relationships: Direct link to packs and cabin inflow. Cross-feeds with APU via the isolation valve.
controls: BLEED 1 / BLEED 2. BLEED TRIP OFF, MASTER CAUTION, AIR COND.

name: Bleed Air Check Valve
function: Prevents back-pressurization of the 8th-stage bleed port.
flow: In the 8th-stage line upstream of the precooler.
relationships: Isolates 8th/13th stage from APU or ground cart reverse flow.

name: Bleed Air Heat Exchanger (Precooler)
function: Cools ~520°F compressor bleed with fan discharge air.
flow: Bleed through core; fan air through matrix, overboard via the precooler valve. Target ~370–450°F.
relationships: Feeds the engine bleed valve. Protected by the 490°F overheat switch.
controls: Shares BLEED TRIP OFF with the bleed valve.

name: Pressure Ratio Bleed Control
function: Operates compressor surge-bleed valves from front-compressor pressure ratio.
flow: Senses Pt2 and Ps3 → pilot valve → Ps4 air to surge valves → dump to fan stream.
relationships: Prevents stall/surge at low-to-mid power.

name: Modulating and Shutoff Valve
function: Regulates 13th-stage high-pressure bleed into the manifold; shuts off when 8th-stage is enough.
flow: 13th-stage duct → MSOV → merges with 8th-stage upstream of the precooler.
relationships: Works with the 450°F thermostat.
controls: Automatic; tied to BLEED TRIP OFF logic.

name: Thrust Reverser Deflector Doors
function: Clamshell doors that redirect exhaust forward and outboard for reverse thrust.
flow: Hydraulic actuators via overcenter linkages. Held closed by mechanical locks.
relationships: Ground only. REVERSER UNLOCKED lights when doors leave stowed.
controls: Reverser lever with interlocks. REVERSER UNLOCKED light.

name: Thrust Reverser Lock
function: Mechanical latch holding deflector doors stowed until hydraulic pressure is applied.
flow: Pressure unlocks the latch slightly before actuator extension. Proximity sensor reports door status.
relationships: Sensor drives REVERSER UNLOCKED.

name: Thrust Reverser Isolation Valve
function: Solenoid valve controlling Hyd A supply to the reverser system.
flow: Opens only when fire switch, oil pressure, and air/ground interlocks are satisfied.
relationships: Spring-loaded closed; controlled by air-ground, engine-running/low-oil-pressure and fire-switch inputs.
controls: ISOLATION VALVE light. ENG 1/2 THRUST REVERSER CBs on P6.

name: Thrust Reverser Actuators
function: Hydraulic linear actuators driving deflector door linkages.
flow: Hyd A → isolation valve → directional valve → extend to deploy / retract to stow.
relationships: Normally supplied by System A; aircraft with the standby connection can use standby hydraulic pressure through shuttle valves as the alternate source.
controls: Reverser lever once isolation is open.

name: Engine Fuel Heat Exchanger
function: Represents the engine fuel heat-exchanger assembly. The linked ATA 28 fuel-heater control-path entry models the simulator switch, available power, valve indication and temperature response.
flow: Fuel flows through the heater continuously; 13th-stage compressor bleed air passes through the heater air tubes only when the fuel heat valve is open. A bypass valve permits fuel to bypass the heater if clogged.
relationships: Engine-level hardware representation; do not interpret the simulator thermal response as a verified AMM heater schedule. Downstream fuel-filter icing feedback is represented separately.
controls: Linked to the ATA 28 FUEL HEAT control-path model.

name: Fuel Filter Differential Pressure Switch
function: Detects increased differential pressure across the engine main fuel filter when icing restricts fuel flow.
flow: Senses pressure differential across the main fuel filter; signal is a feedback/indication path, not a fuel-flow component.
relationships: Closes on excessive differential pressure to illuminate the fuel filter icing indication and master caution; opens again after the ice is melted.
controls: Feeds FUEL FILTER ICING indication and fuel-heating logic.

name: Engine Fuel Control Unit
function: Meters and regulates engine fuel flow in response to the engine control system.
flow: Aircraft engine fuel supply → engine-driven fuel pumping/control stages → fuel control unit → engine fuel manifold/nozzles.
relationships: Mechanically commanded by the engine control system; receives fuel from the aircraft fuel system and interfaces with the fuel/oil cooler and fuel-flow indication.
controls: Thrust control and start-lever interfaces; engine fuel shutoff is a separate aircraft-fuel-system isolation function.

name: Engine Thrust Control
function: Transfers forward thrust-lever movement through the engine control mechanism to regulate fuel flow and forward thrust.
flow: Thrust lever → control drum/cables/push-pull linkage → engine fuel control unit.
relationships: Separate control path from physical fuel flow. Reverse-thrust control uses the same general cable/linkage system but drives the reverser function in the reverse direction.
controls: THRUST LEVER and reverse-thrust lever; mechanical lockout prevents simultaneous forward and reverse thrust commands.

name: Engine Start Control
function: Uses the engine start lever and associated control mechanism to initiate ignition and fuel introduction or shut off fuel as applicable to effectivity.
flow: Start lever → start control shaft/drum/switches → ignition enable and engine fuel-control/start functions.
relationships: Interfaces with ATA 74 ignition and ATA 73 fuel control; fuel introduction is performed only after starter rotation is established.

name: EPR Pressure Sensing & Transmitter
function: Converts engine inlet Pt2 and exhaust Pt7 pressures into an engine pressure ratio signal for the cockpit EPR indicator.
flow: Pt2 nose-dome probe + Pt7 exhaust probes → EPR transmitter → three-phase signal → EPR indicator.
relationships: Indication/feedback only; not inserted into the engine airflow path. Pt2 probe is protected by engine anti-ice.
controls: EPR circuit breaker; EPR indicator provides pointer/digital readout.

name: EGT Thermocouple System
function: Measures engine exhaust gas temperature using eight thermocouple probes and sends the averaged signal to the cockpit EGT indicator.
flow: Eight exhaust thermocouple probes in parallel → harness/lead → EGT indicator.
relationships: Pure indication/feedback branch; it does not alter exhaust flow.

name: Engine Oil Pressure System
function: Supplies pressure oil to engine bearings and accessory drives and returns scavenged oil to the tank.
flow: Oil tank → engine-driven pressure pump → oil filter → fuel/oil cooler → engine bearings/accessories → scavenge pumps → accessory gearbox sump → pump scavenge stage → oil tank.
relationships: Closed-loop lubrication system with separate breather path. Filter and cooler bypass valves preserve oil flow if restricted.
controls: Oil pressure/temperature indications and low-oil-pressure warning.

name: Engine 1 Magnetic Chip Detector
function: Magnetic detector monitoring ferrous debris in the engine oil system.
flow: Oil system debris → magnetic chip detector → cockpit maintenance indication.
relationships: Discrete maintenance indication; detection does not by itself command an automatic engine shutdown.

name: Engine 2 Magnetic Chip Detector
function: Magnetic detector monitoring ferrous debris in the engine oil system.
flow: Oil system debris → magnetic chip detector → cockpit maintenance indication.
relationships: Discrete maintenance indication; detection does not by itself command an automatic engine shutdown.

name: Engine Oil Indications
function: Provides oil quantity, pressure, temperature and low-pressure/bypass status indications.
flow: Oil tank/system sensing units → cockpit oil quantity/pressure/temperature indications and warning circuits.
relationships: Separate feedback branches from the physical oil circulation loop.
controls: Oil Temperature and Pressure circuit breaker; cockpit indicators/warnings.

name: Pneumatic Start Air Sources
function: Provides the low-pressure air sources used to rotate the engine during starting.
flow: APU bleed OR ground pneumatic source OR operating-engine cross-bleed → pneumatic manifold → starter valve.
relationships: Source selection belongs to the pneumatic/start interface; the starter itself remains a pneumatic load, not an AC electrical load.
controls: Engine start switches plus pneumatic/bleed controls required for the selected source.

name: Engine Installation / Nacelle Interface
function: Represents the aircraft-to-engine installation interface, including nacelle/cowl access and system interfaces.
flow: Structural and system interface node; not a fluid or electrical flow stage.
relationships: Interfaces with engine controls, bleed, fuel, hydraulic, electrical, exhaust and thrust-reverser systems.
controls: Maintenance/access interfaces rather than a normal cockpit control.

name: Hydraulic Ground Servicing Pump
function: Hand pump used during ground hydraulic fluid servicing.
flow: Draws fluid from the central servicing supply and discharges through the servicing filter into the shared reservoir fill/balance lines.
relationships: Ground servicing fills System A, System B, and Standby reservoirs through the shared balance manifold; it is separate from ground hydraulic power/interconnect pressure.

name: Hydraulic Servicing Filter
function: Filters hydraulic fluid during ground servicing.
flow: Downstream of the ground servicing pump and pressure-fill port, upstream of the shared reservoir fill/balance manifold.
relationships: Protects System A, System B, and Standby reservoirs equally during fluid servicing.

name: Hydraulic Ground Power Modular Unit
function: Pressure/return QDs so a ground cart can power systems without engines or electric pumps.
flow: External pressure into System B; with ground interconnect open, pressure extends to A.
relationships: Used with the ground interconnect valve.

name: Ground Interconnect Valve
function: Motor-driven valve connecting A and B pressure lines for ground testing.
flow: Normally closed; interlocked via parking brake relay. Internal check prevents A from pressurizing B. Prohibited in flight.
relationships: Enables single-source ground pressurization of both systems.
controls: GROUND INTERCONNECT OPEN/CLOSE. Manual override on the valve. CB on P6.

name: System A Engine-Driven Pump
function: Variable-displacement, pressure-compensated pump providing primary 3000 psi for System A.
flow: Reservoir → supply shutoff → pump → pressure filter → System A module. Pump case drain → No. 1 fuel-tank heat exchanger → reservoir.
relationships: Driven by both engine accessory gearboxes. Needs ~40–47 psi reservoir head.
controls: ENG 1 / ENG 2 HYD PUMP. Low pressure lights below ~1200 psi.

name: System A Pressure Filter — Engine 1
function: Filters pressure fluid downstream of the No. 1 engine-driven hydraulic pump before entry to the System A module.
flow: ENG 1 EDP → pressure filter → System A module.
relationships: Protects the System A module and downstream hydraulic users from pump-side contamination.

name: System A Pressure Filter — Engine 2
function: Filters pressure fluid downstream of the No. 2 engine-driven hydraulic pump before entry to the System A module.
flow: ENG 2 EDP → pressure filter → System A module.
relationships: Protects the System A module and downstream hydraulic users from pump-side contamination.

name: System A Hydraulic Reservoir
function: Stores and conditions System A fluid with bleed-air pressurization.
flow: Feeds engine pumps via shutoffs; receives main system return through the return filter. Pump case-drain fluid is cooled in the No. 1 fuel-tank heat exchanger before reservoir return.
relationships: Tied to B and Standby reservoirs through the shared pneumatic pressurization and fluid servicing balance lines.
controls: Quantity transmitter to the FO hydraulic quantity indicator.

name: Hydraulic System A Module Unit
function: Left wheel-well manifold: filters, relief, low-pressure switches, check valves.
flow: Consolidates both engine-pump outputs and distributes System A hydraulic pressure to its assigned users.
relationships: Primary power for landing gear and reversers.
controls: Monitored via low-pressure lights and quantity.

name: Hydraulic Supply Fire Shutoff Valve
function: Motor-driven sliding gate isolating fluid to the engine nacelle in a fire.
flow: Between System A reservoir suction and the engine-driven pump inlet.
relationships: Actuated by the engine fire handle with fuel and pneumatic shutoffs.
controls: ENG 1 / ENG 2 FIRE handles. Visual OPEN/CLOSED on the valve.

name: System A Return Filter
function: Filters return fluid before reservoir re-entry, with auto-bypass.
flow: Main System A return, immediately upstream of the reservoir.
relationships: Final conditioning stage for A.
controls: Pop-up ΔP button on the filter head.

name: System B Hydraulic Reservoir
function: Stores fluid for System B electric pumps. Heat exchanger in tank No. 2.
flow: Supplies B AC pumps; receives return via filter and fuel-tank HX.
relationships: Complements A; shares reservoir pressurization manifold.

name: System B Electric Motor-Driven Pumps
function: Two 115V AC pumps providing 3000 psi for B loads (brakes, flight-control backup).
flow: B reservoir → pumps → B distribution.
relationships: Primary B source; redundant with A for many flight controls.
controls: ELEC 1 / ELEC 2 HYD PUMP. Low pressure lights.

name: System B Module Unit
function: Right wheel-well manifold for B protective and sensing components.
flow: Receives System B pressure from the two electric pump outlets through the System B pressure manifold, then distributes it to the primary flight-control module, outboard flight spoilers, and main-wheel outboard brakes.
relationships: B equivalent of the A module.
controls: ELEC 1/2 LOW PRESSURE lights. SYSTEM A-B PRESSURE CB on P6.

name: Standby Hydraulic Pump
function: Electric pump providing backup ~3000 psi for rudder and LE flaps/slats when A is lost.
flow: Standby reservoir → pump → standby network on auto or manual activation.
relationships: AUTO with System A low pressure. Serves flight-control essential users.
controls: STANDBY HYD PUMP AUTO/ON/OFF. STBY RUD ON light. CBs C847/C848.

name: Standby Hydraulic Reservoir
function: Dedicated reservoir for the standby electric pump and ground servicing fill path.
flow: Ground servicing pump → servicing filter → shared fill/balance manifold → standby reservoir → standby pump; receives direct standby-load return.
relationships: Filled and pressurized through the common A/B/Standby reservoir interfaces described in ATA 29.

name: Standby Hydraulic Modular Unit
function: Aft wheel-well manifold for standby relief, filters, and low-pressure switch.
flow: Between standby pump and rudder / LE device actuators. ~2900 ± 100 psi.
relationships: Standby users: rudder and leading-edge flaps/slats.

name: Reservoir Pressurization Regulator
function: Regulates engine bleed air used to pressurize all three hydraulic reservoirs and maintain positive pump inlet head.
flow: Engine bleed → air filter → pressure regulator → common reservoir pressurization manifold → A / B / Standby reservoirs.
relationships: Common pneumatic supply for all three hydraulic systems; separate from the hydraulic-fluid servicing manifold.

name: Hydraulic Reservoir Pressurization Relief Valve
function: Protects the common reservoir pressurization manifold and all three hydraulic reservoirs from excessive air pressure.
flow: Reservoir pressurization manifold → relief valve → vent when pressure exceeds the protected limit.
relationships: Final safety device in the common A/B/Standby reservoir pressurization system.

name: Inertial Air Cleaner
function: Removes dust and sand from engine bleed air before pneumatic distribution.
flow: Engine bleed → precooler → inertial air cleaner → clean air to pneumatic manifold; collected particles to purge circuit.
relationships: Purge branch is separate from the conditioned-air path and exhausts through the ram/turbofan exhaust system.

name: Hot-Air Bypass Duct
function: Provides warm bypass air around the air-cycle cooling path for temperature mixing.
flow: Pack valve / mix valve bypass branch → mixing chamber.
relationships: Parallel to the ACM cooling path; it is not routed through the ACM compressor or turbine.

name: Mixing Chamber
function: Combines cooled air and hot bypass air before cabin distribution.
flow: Water separator cold-air output + hot-air bypass → mixing chamber → main distribution manifold.
relationships: Downstream of the Air Mix Valve and upstream of the main distribution manifold.
controls: Temperature-control system regulates the mix upstream.

name: Pack Valve
function: Pneumatically-driven, electrically-controlled shutoff/flow-control into each pack.
flow: Manifold → pack valve (venturi-scheduled) → hot-air duct → mix valve / ACM. Closure drives mix valve full cold.
relationships: Downstream of engine or APU bleed. Higher flow scheduled on APU bleed. Output is cabin inflow.
controls: L PACK / R PACK on P5-10. PACK TRIP OFF → MASTER CAUTION + AIR COND.

name: Ground Service Conditioned-Air Connection
function: Supplies conditioned air directly to the main distribution manifold when the airplane air-conditioning packs are off.
flow: Ground conditioned-air cart → service connection/check valve → main distribution manifold → control and passenger cabins.
relationships: Check valve closes when aircraft pack air is supplying the manifold.

name: Engine Bleed Isolation Valve
function: Connects or isolates left and right pneumatic manifolds.
flow: In the cross-manifold duct. OPEN/AUTO cross-feeds; CLOSE isolates. Normal is AUTO.
relationships: Interlocks with BLEED 1/2 and APU BLEED. DUAL BLEED guards dual-source mistakes.
controls: ISOLATION VALVE OPEN/AUTO/CLOSE on P5-10. DUAL BLEED light.

name: Air Cleaner Purge Valve
function: Vents dust/sand collected by the inertial cleaner into the ram exhaust.
flow: Downstream of the precooler. Opens on engine bleed on the ground or with flaps extended.
relationships: Shares control and exhaust ducting with the turbofan/ram system.
controls: Automatic. TURBOFAN VALVE CB on P6. Mechanical position indicator.

name: Primary & Secondary Heat Exchangers
function: Air-to-air exchangers cooling bleed with ram air (flight) or turbofan air (ground).
flow: Primary before ACM compressor; secondary after compressor, before the turbine.
relationships: Blockage shows up as high supply-duct temperature.
controls: Monitored via SUPPLY DUCT on AIR TEMP selector P5-17.

name: Air Cycle Machine
function: Turbine, compressor, and fan on a common shaft — the pack’s refrigeration core.
flow: Primary HX → compressor → secondary HX → expansion turbine → water separator.
relationships: All pack cooling hardware exists to support or modulate ACM output.
controls: Runs when PACK is ON with bleed available. Sump checked on the ground.

name: Water Separator
function: Removes moisture condensed after ACM expansion so water does not enter cabin ducts.
flow: Wet cold air through the coalescer bag; water drains overboard.
relationships: Feeds the 35°F control valve, whose sensor lives at the separator.
controls: Red/black bag condition band — maintenance only.

name: Water Separator Coalescer Bag
function: Filter media that coalesces fine droplets so they can drain.
flow: All cooled moist air passes through it before the 35°F valve.
relationships: A clogged bag causes high flow readings on ground checks and poor moisture removal.

name: 35-Degree F Control Valve
function: Anti-ice valve blending warm air around the separator to hold ~35°F.
flow: Opens as separator discharge approaches freezing; modulates at equilibrium.
relationships: Valve position (full open vs modulating) is a primary pack-efficiency diagnostic.

name: Turbofan
function: Air-turbine fan pulling cooling air through the heat exchangers on the ground.
flow: Spun by high-pressure air metered through the turbofan valve; exhausts overboard.
relationships: Paired with the turbofan valve. Makes the HX effective without ram air.
controls: Automatic. L/R TURBOFAN CBs on P6. Dipstick oil check.

name: Turbofan Valve
function: Meters duct air to spin the turbofan; closes once ram air takes over.
flow: Opens when duct pressure is ~27–33 psi; closes as speed/ram rises.
relationships: Shares the ram exhaust duct with the air cleaner purge valve.
controls: Automatic. TURBOFAN VALVE CB on P6.

name: Air Mix Valve
function: Proportions hot bleed with ACM-cold air to the selected cabin/cockpit temperature.
flow: At the hot-bypass / cold-delivery junction. Driven full cold on pack valve closure.
relationships: Final pack thermal element. Supplies the volume the outflow valve then meters.
controls: CONT CABIN / PASS CABIN selectors on P5-17. Mix valve position indicators.

name: Cabin Pressurization Outflow Valve
function: Meters cabin exhaust to control cabin altitude and differential.
flow: AUTO / STANDBY / MAN AC / MAN DC drive the valve. Packs provide inflow; this is outflow.
relationships: Backup is the safety relief valve. Inflow traces to pack valves and engine/APU bleed.
controls: MODE SELECTOR and OPEN/CLOSE on P5-6. Valve position, DIFF PRESS, cabin alt/rate. Horn ~10,000 ft.

name: Safety Relief Valve Left
function: Independent mechanical overpressure protection on the left side of the outflow valve.
flow: Cabin differential pressure above limit → safety relief valve → overboard.
relationships: Independent of AUTO/STANDBY/MAN outflow-valve control.

name: Safety Relief Valve Right
function: Independent mechanical overpressure protection on the right side of the outflow valve.
flow: Cabin differential pressure above limit → safety relief valve → overboard.
relationships: Independent of AUTO/STANDBY/MAN outflow-valve control.

name: Negative / Vacuum Relief Valve
function: Protects the fuselage from excessive negative cabin-to-ambient differential pressure.
flow: Ambient pressure greater than cabin pressure → negative relief valve → cabin.
relationships: Independent mechanical protection during rapid descent or loss of cabin air input.

name: Safety Relief Valve
function: Spring-loaded relief protecting the fuselage if outflow control fails.
flow: Opens ~8–8.5 psi differential, vents overboard, reseats.
relationships: Backup to the outflow valve control loop.

name: Passenger Water Tank
function: Stores potable water for galleys and lavatory faucets.
flow: Filled at the service panel; pressurized by No. 1 engine bleed through a dedicated regulator.
relationships: Feeds quantity transmitter, filter, and heater. Separate from the hydraulic reservoir regulator.
controls: Service-panel handles. WATER QTY IND CB on P18.

name: Water Quantity Transmitter
function: Float switches reporting Empty / 1/4 / 1/2 / 3/4 / Full.
flow: Float in a tube energizes indicator segments.
relationships: Sensing only — no control.
controls: Indicator on the aft right service door. WATER QTY IND CB P18.

name: Water Filter
function: Charcoal cartridge removing dirt, colloids, and chlorine taste from cold water.
flow: Under the lavatory basin in the cold supply.
relationships: Between tank and cold tap.

name: Water Heater
function: 1.5-quart, 400 W heater per lavatory hot tap. Thermostat ~125°F; overheat ~190°F.
flow: Three-probe element in a small tank; overheat switch is manually reset.
relationships: Hot side of the same plumbing the filter conditions on the cold side.
controls: Heater ON/OFF and amber light on the tank. LAVATORY WATER HEATER CB P18.

name: Toilet Flush Motor
function: Combined motor, pump, and filter that flushes the bowl.
flow: Timer-commanded impeller draws ~2 gal from the waste tank through a filter and the flush ring.
relationships: Runs only when the toilet timer powers it.
controls: LAV FLUSH MOTOR CB on P18 (one per lav).

name: Toilet Timer
function: Electromechanical timer that powers the flush motor for 10 ± 2 seconds.
flow: Flush handle ~15° actuates the timer, which then feeds 115V AC to the motor.
relationships: Between handle and motor.

name: Toilet Waste Tank
function: Holds waste and flush fluid; one-piece bowl/tank.
flow: Drains via a cable-actuated service-panel handle to a ground cart.
relationships: Reservoir the flush motor draws from and returns to.
controls: Mechanical cable. Open LAV FLUSH MOTOR CB while servicing.

name: Passenger Service Unit
function: Overhead unit with reading lights, attendant call, oxygen masks, and gaspers.
flow: Passenger-switched lights/call; oxygen doors on barometric drop or crew override.
relationships: Shares cabin lighting and oxygen architecture.
controls: Passenger switches. Oxygen auto or flight-deck override.

name: Passenger Cabin Windows
function: Dual acrylic panes containing cabin differential while providing visibility.
flow: Breather hole in the middle pane manages interpane pressure.
relationships: Must hold the same ΔP the outflow and safety valves regulate.

name: Window No. 2 (Pilot Sliding Window)
function: Hand-operated sliding side window for ground ventilation, lookout, and emergency egress, with a 28V heater.
flow: Locking handle; heater independent of the sliding function.
relationships: Distinct from fixed cabin windows.
controls: Window heat CBs — no dedicated sliding-window switch.

name: Flight Controls Hydraulic Modular Package
function: Wheel-well manifold housing flight-control and spoiler shutoff valves, compensator, check, and low-pressure switch.
flow: A/B pressure → FC shutoff to aileron/elevator/rudder and spoiler shutoff to flight spoilers. Return through compensator (gust damper residual).
relationships: All hydraulic flight-control actuators depend on package activation. Adjacent to A/B module units.
controls: FLIGHT CONTROLS A/B & SPOILER A/B on P5-3. LOW PRESSURE lights + MASTER CAUTION.

name: Aileron
function: Hinged wingtip surfaces providing primary roll, deflecting symmetrically opposite.
flow: Control wheel → cables → dual-powered PCUs → surface. Balance tabs refine feel.
relationships: Same wheel input commands flight spoilers for roll augmentation.
controls: Control wheel; gated by FLIGHT CONTROLS A/B.

name: Flight Spoiler
function: Four upper-wing panels for roll assist or symmetric speed-brake drag.
flow: Hydraulic actuator from aileron system and/or speed-brake lever.
relationships: Gated by spoiler shutoff valves. On ground with lever full up, 2/3/6/7 match ground spoilers.

name: Ground Spoiler Actuator Valve
function: Controls Hyd A flow to ground spoilers for lift dump on landing or RTO.
flow: Armed via speed-brake ARMED → deploys on WOW or lever UP.
relationships: In series with the ground spoiler interlock valve (prevents in-flight deploy).
controls: SPEED BRAKE ARMED light; speed-brake lever.

name: No. 1 and No. 8 Ground Spoilers
function: Outermost ground-only panels dumping lift to maximize wheel braking.
flow: Locked out in flight by the interlock valve.
relationships: Work with flight spoilers and inboard ground spoilers 4 and 5.

name: Flap Power Unit
function: Hydraulic motor plus electric backup on a differential gearbox driving TE flap torque tubes.
flow: Flap lever → cables → flap control valve → hydraulic motor → torque tubes.
relationships: Primary Hyd A, backup 115V AC electric drive.
controls: Flap lever; ALTERNATE FLAPS ARM & POSITION on P5-3.

name: Flap Hydraulic Motor
function: Primary rotary drive inside the flap power unit.
flow: Metered System A from the flap control valve.
relationships: Physically combined with the electric standby motor.
controls: SHUTOFF VALVES – FLAP CB on P6.

name: Leading Edge Flaps
function: Inboard leading-edge panels that increase camber for takeoff/landing.
flow: Flap lever → LE flap & slat control valve → actuators. Backup from standby hydraulics.
relationships: Synchronous with outboard LE slats and trailing-edge flaps.
controls: Flap lever; ALTERNATE FLAPS triggers standby pump.

name: Elevator Control Unit
function: Interfaces column, stabilizer trim, and elevator PCU inputs.
flow: Column → ECU → A/B PCUs → elevator.
relationships: Works with the elevator feel computer.

name: Elevator Feel Computer
function: Uses pitot-static q and stabilizer position to set artificial column force.
flow: Pitot + stab position → feel computer → hydraulic feel unit → column.
relationships: Feel scales with dynamic pressure.
controls: FEEL DIFF PRESS light on P5-3.

name: Landing Gear Selector Valve
function: Directs System A to retract or extend main and nose gear.
flow: LANDING GEAR lever → cable/drum → selector quadrant → actuators, uplocks, downlocks.
relationships: Upstream of all extension actuators. Powered only by System A.
controls: LANDING GEAR lever. LEVER LATCH CB on P6.

name: Main Gear Isolation Valve
function: Isolates left and right main-gear supply during a leak.
flow: Two-position; normal OPEN. Closed manually in maintenance.
relationships: Downstream of the selector, upstream of main-gear actuators.
controls: No cockpit switch. Lockwire on the handle stop.

name: Main Gear Modular Package
function: Cartridge manifold (relief, check, restrictors) for main-gear servicing.
flow: Between selector/isolation and actuating/locking mechanisms.
relationships: Main-gear equivalent of the nose-gear modular package.

name: Captain Nose-Wheel Steering Tiller
function: Provides normal nose-wheel steering command.
flow: Captain steering tiller → steering cables / metering valve → nose-wheel steering actuators.
relationships: Primary steering input; available with nose gear down and steering system enabled.

name: Rudder-Pedal Nose-Wheel Steering
function: Provides reduced-range nose-wheel steering from rudder pedal input.
flow: Rudder pedals → steering mechanism / cables → nose-wheel steering actuators.
relationships: Separate reduced-range control path from the captain steering wheel.

name: Steering Depressurization Valve
function: Routes System A to nose-wheel steering when gear is down and WOW.
flow: Interlocked with air/ground and gear position — no airborne steering.
relationships: Tiller and rudder pedals provide the input.

name: Hydraulic Brakes Accumulator
function: Stores pressurized fluid for reserve braking if pump pressure is lost.
flow: Charged by System B; routes reserve via the autobrake shuttle when normal pressure drops.
relationships: Independent of continuous pump pressure.
controls: Brake pressure gauges on the center panel.

name: Hydraulic Brakes Pressure Transmitter
function: Converts brake-line pressure to electrical signals for the dual brake indicator.
flow: Senses System B brake pressure.
relationships: Center panel P2-2 indication.

name: Autobrake Shuttle Valve
function: Routes automatic-brake pressure into the brake circuit while preserving the manual brake path.
flow: Autobrake pressure control module → shuttle valves → brake units through antiskid valves.
relationships: Autobrake bypasses the pilot metering-valve command; antiskid remains in series and has priority for skid protection.

name: Autobrake Pressure Control Module
function: Meters pressure to the selected automatic deceleration rate, including RTO.
flow: Cockpit selector → module → shuttle valves.
relationships: Works with anti-skid.
controls: AUTOBRAKE selector on the center panel.

name: Anti-Skid Transducer
function: Wheel-speed transducers on each braked wheel.
flow: Electrical signal proportional to wheel speed → anti-skid control unit.
relationships: Primary input for lock-up detection.
controls: ANTISKID status. Failure via master caution.

name: Anti-Skid Control Valve
function: Modulates automatic or manual brake pressure to prevent wheel lock/skid.
flow: Brake pressure command → antiskid valve → wheel brake; antiskid can override automatic-brake pressure.
relationships: Both inboard and outboard antiskid channels must be operative for autobrake operation.
controls: INBD / OUTBD ANTISKID switches on P2-2.

name: Engine Anti-Ice Valve
function: Controls pneumatic thermal anti-ice air supplied to the engine inlet/nose-dome anti-ice system.
flow: Engine compressor bleed air → anti-ice valve/control → engine inlet/nose-dome internal ducting → anti-ice exhaust.
relationships: Separate from wing anti-ice. Controlled by the ENG ANTI-ICE switch; valve position is indicated by ANTI-ICE VALVE OPEN.
controls: ENG ANTI-ICE switch on P5; ANTI-ICE VALVE OPEN indication.

name: Left Wing Anti-Ice Valve / Thermal System
function: Controls thermal anti-ice air to the left wing leading-edge anti-ice system.
flow: Pneumatic manifold → left wing anti-ice valve → left wing thermal anti-ice ducts/surfaces.
relationships: Has separate valve-open indication and thermal feedback; does not form a series path with the right wing system.
controls: WING ANTI-ICE switch; left VALVE OPEN indication.

name: Right Wing Anti-Ice Valve / Thermal System
function: Controls thermal anti-ice air to the right wing leading-edge anti-ice system.
flow: Pneumatic manifold → right wing anti-ice valve → right wing thermal anti-ice ducts/surfaces.
relationships: Has separate valve-open indication and thermal feedback; does not form a series path with the left wing system.
controls: WING ANTI-ICE switch; right VALVE OPEN indication.

name: Wing Anti-Ice Thermal Feedback
function: Provides thermal status feedback for wing anti-ice control logic.
flow: Wing thermal switch/sensor → anti-ice control/feedback logic.
relationships: Feedback path only; it is not in the pneumatic airflow path.

name: Pitot / Static / TAT Ice Protection
function: Protects critical air-data probe and port areas from icing; modeled independently from wing/engine bleed-air paths.
flow: Electrical/thermal protection and air-data sensing remain separate from the wing and engine pneumatic anti-ice branches.
relationships: Feeds/affects air-data sensing rather than acting as a downstream pneumatic load.
controls: System-dependent; status represented separately from thermal bleed-air flow.

name: Bleed-Air Pneumatic Manifold
function: Receives conditioned engine/APU bleed air and distributes it to approved pneumatic users.
flow: Engine/APU bleed sources → isolation/manifold → pack and starter users.
relationships: Isolation-valve logic selects the manifold arrangement; sources must not be treated as a single undifferentiated switch.

name: Pneumatic Isolation Valve
function: Controls interconnection between left and right bleed-air manifolds.
flow: Left manifold ↔ isolation valve ↔ right manifold.
relationships: AUTO mode is governed by the bleed/pack switch configuration; the switch, not an inferred valve position, is the command authority.

name: Bleed-Air Precooler Assembly
function: Reduces hot compressor bleed-air temperature before manifold distribution using fan air.
flow: Engine bleed takeoff → precooler → bleed manifold.
relationships: Bleed pressure and overheat logic depend on source condition and cooling path; this is a training-level representation.
controls: Engine bleed and precooler control logic

name: Pneumatic Duct Pressure Indication
function: Displays available bleed-manifold pressure for start-air and air-conditioning training.
flow: Pressure sensing point → cockpit indication.
relationships: Indication must respond to modeled source pressure and the relevant electrical supply.

name: No. 1 Generator Drive / CSD
function: Models the engine accessory drive and generator-drive disconnect for the No. 1 electrical source.
flow: Engine accessory gearbox → CSD/drive → generator → generator breaker.
relationships: DISC operates a separate drive-disconnect state and does not silently reset the GEN switch; oil-pressure and oil-temperature indications are separate paths.

name: No. 2 Generator Drive / CSD
function: Models the engine accessory drive and generator-drive disconnect for the No. 2 electrical source.
flow: Engine accessory gearbox → CSD/drive → generator → generator breaker.
relationships: DISC operates a separate drive-disconnect state; oil indications are modeled separately from generator-bus power.

name: Cabin Recirculation / Gasper Fan
function: Provides a modeled recirculation contribution when selected and AC power is available.
flow: Cabin return air → fan → cabin air distribution.
relationships: Fan power/load and airflow contribution are separate from pack valve selection; failure removes the contribution.

name: Equipment Cooling Supply / Exhaust Blowers
function: Models the electrical power and failure state of the supply and exhaust cooling blower paths.
flow: Cabin/equipment-space air → supply blower → avionics/equipment flow path → exhaust blower.
relationships: Supply and exhaust selectors are maintained independently; NORM/ALTN are not interpreted as OFF.

name: Continuous-Cabin Air Mix Valve
function: Stores a continuous manual mix position for the control-cabin air-mix valve.
flow: Pack cooling path + hot bypass → left/control-cabin mix valve → distribution.
relationships: AUTO uses the simplified regulator schedule; MANUAL uses the stored position; a valve-jam fault freezes the effective position.

name: Passenger-Cabin Air Mix Valve
function: Stores a continuous manual mix position for the passenger-cabin air-mix valve.
flow: Pack cooling path + hot bypass → passenger-cabin mix valve → cabin distribution.
relationships: Separate state and jam fault from the control-cabin valve; position indication follows the modeled valve position.

name: Fuel Heating Valve / Control Path
function: Models separate engine fuel-heater selection, the WDM-confirmed 28V DC Bus 1 / Bus 2 control feeds, valve-open indication and trainer fuel-temperature response.
flow: ENG 1 command + 28V DC Bus 1 / ENG 2 command + 28V DC Bus 2 → separate heater valve/timer paths → modeled fuel temperature response.
relationships: Failure can inhibit heating; temperature-rise rate is trainer-defined and must not be treated as an AMM calibration value.

name: Fuel Temperature Indication
function: Displays fuel temperature in tank No.1 when its 28V AC Bus No.2 indication circuit is powered; loss of power parks the pointer off scale at the low end.
flow: Tank No.1 sensing bulb → P5-2 fuel-temperature indicator; power through P6-3 C355 from 28V AC Bus No.2.
relationships: The supplied WDM calls this subject 28-42-01 (sheet 21 for effectivity 359); AMM D6-12005 calls the description 28-43-0. Preserve this cross-manual ATA numbering discrepancy in audit records.
controls: FUEL TEMP gauge / P6-3 C355 indication circuit

name: Windshield / Window Heat Electrical Groups
function: Models the left and right window-heat power groups and their heating effect on the visual ice/fog state.
flow: AC source → window heat group → windshield/window thermal state.
relationships: Overheat cutout and injected channel failure can inhibit heating; detailed channel-to-window effectivity remains a WDM check item.

name: Rain Repellent Spray System
function: Converts a momentary left/right command into a timed spray pulse and visible pane-repellent animation.
flow: P5 spray command → timed control pulse → selected windshield pane.
relationships: Left and right pulses are independent; failure inhibits both modeled spray paths.

name: Yaw Damper Actuator / Signal Path
function: Applies training-level yaw-rate damping when selected, DC powered, hydraulic pressure is available and no injected fault is active.
flow: Yaw rate + yaw-damper command → damping law → rudder/yaw response.
relationships: Power and System B hydraulic interlocks are distinct from the command switch; the damping gain is a simulator approximation.

name: Crew Oxygen Supply / Pressure Indication
function: Models crew oxygen bottle pressure, the crew NORMAL/ON selection and pressure-indication power/failure.
flow: Crew oxygen bottle → regulator/mask supply → pressure indication and simulated mask-mic interlock.
relationships: Pressure usage/leak rates are trainer values, not a specified AMM flow/pressure schedule.

name: Passenger Oxygen System Control
function: Models NORMAL/ON selection and an optional automatic deployment trainer trigger.
flow: Passenger oxygen command / simulated cabin-altitude threshold → deployed indication.
relationships: Threshold estimation is simplified; distribution and detailed passenger service-unit deployment are not fully represented.

name: Left Inertial Reference Unit (Training Model)
function: Models OFF/ALIGN/NAV/ATT selection, DC-gated alignment progress and left-side heading validity.
flow: DC power → IRS align state → heading/attitude source-validity path.
relationships: This is an intentionally simplified IRS training model; it is not a full calibrated inertial navigation solution.

name: Right Inertial Reference Unit (Training Model)
function: Models OFF/ALIGN/NAV/ATT selection, DC-gated alignment progress and right-side heading validity.
flow: DC power → IRS align state → heading/attitude source-validity path.
relationships: This is an intentionally simplified IRS training model; it is not a full calibrated inertial navigation solution.

name: Cockpit Voice Recorder Control / Indication
function: Models recorder power, OFF indication, TEST input, elapsed powered-recording time and ground-only erase state.
flow: DC power → CVR control → recorder state and indications.
relationships: Recorded audio content is not captured; state is for system-training behavior only.

name: Cabin Door Warning Indication
function: Drives a common door-warning indication from the shared simulated door-position state and opens a qualitative cabin-pressure leak path when a modeled door is open.
flow: Modeled door position → warning logic and pressure leak → DOOR WARN indication / cabin differential decay.
relationships: Per-door annunciations and pressure-leak response are training-level approximations; failure suppresses the annunciation but does not close the door or leak path.

name: Emergency Locator Transmitter
function: Models OFF/ARM/ON selection, manual transmission and a simplified overrun/impact cue in ARM.
flow: ELT selector / event cue → transmitter state → ELT indication.
relationships: No RF signal is transmitted by this trainer; event logic is for visual instruction only.

name: Service Interphone / Cabin Call
function: Models service-interphone selection, attendant/ground calls and the shared call indication.
flow: Call button → shared SimState call flag → powered cabin CALL indication.
relationships: Audio routing is not full aircraft interphone wiring; all visible trainer panels share a single state.

name: Exterior Lighting Control and Loads
function: Represents exterior lighting command and power distribution for panel/library tracing.
flow: Power bus → lighting control → position/landing/taxi/anti-collision loads.
relationships: Actual per-light state remains driven by deriveLights; this catalog entry is a grouping, not an extra logic engine.

name: Interior / Instrument Lighting Loads
function: Represents panel, flood, cabin and sign lighting circuits in the component library.
flow: Lighting bus → dimmer/selector → interior illumination loads.
relationships: Lighting load details are aggregated in the trainer; individual circuits are not a complete P6 schematic.
controls: PANEL / FLOOD / cabin and sign controls

name: VHF NAV Receiver / Source Transfer Path
function: Links simulated NAV 1/2 receiver state to the MIP receiver selection and guidance validity path.
flow: NAV receiver + selected source → station/ILS geometry → CDI/ADI guidance flags.
relationships: No RF receiver is present; NAV station behavior is software-generated and selection effects are modeled.

name: Stabilizer Trim Cutout / Override
function: Keeps stabilizer trim position, cutout A/B and override in one shared simulation state.
flow: Trim input → cutout/override logic → trim position → pitch-bias training response.
relationships: The trim-to-pitch coefficient is a trainer value; local pedestal trim state no longer overrides the global position.
controls: STAB TRIM / CUTOUT A / CUTOUT B

name: Forward Toilet Drain Heater
function: Models the forward toilet drain heater on the common 115V AC DRAIN HEATER branch.
flow: 115V AC bus No.2 → P18 DRAIN HEATER breaker → forward toilet drain heater.
relationships: WDM 30-71-01, printed sheet 21, effectivity 359 shows the toilet drain heater path; temperature rise is trainer-only.

name: Aft Toilet Drain Heater
function: Models the aft toilet drain heater on the common 115V AC DRAIN HEATER branch.
flow: 115V AC bus No.2 → P18 DRAIN HEATER breaker → aft toilet drain heater.
relationships: WDM 30-71-01, printed sheet 21, effectivity 359 shows the toilet drain heater path; temperature rise is trainer-only.

name: Drain Mast / Drain Line Heaters
function: Models the AIR/GROUND heating feeds for the forward and aft drain-mast elements using the supplied effectivity-359 WDM wire-level bus assignments.
flow: WDM CH30 30-71-01 sheet 21: AIR high heat uses 115V AC BUS No.1 through C700 DRAIN MAST HEATER-AIR; GROUND low heat uses 28V AC BUS No.2 through C224 DRAIN MAST HEATER-GND. Air/ground sensing and external-power inhibition remain modeled. Simulator source selection is resolved to the supplied effectivity-359 WDM (Bus No.1 for AIR mode); AMM ATA 30-71-0 instead names 115V AC Main Bus No.2, so the source-document conflict remains documented and must not be represented as aircraft-configuration-verified.
relationships: WDM 30-71-01 sheet 21, effectivity 359, identifies forward drain mast, forward drain-mast line and aft drain-mast loads. The 28V AC Bus No.2 is represented by a transfer-bus availability proxy; actual temperature/time response remains trainer-only.
specs: 115V AC Bus No.1 air mode per WDM
28V AC Bus No.2 ground mode per WDM
controls: P18 DRAIN MAST HEATER AIR/GROUND CBs

name: Left Alpha-Vane Heater / Ice State
function: Models the left alpha-vane heater power path and qualitative ice accretion/removal state under shared icing conditions.
flow: Icing condition + heater command + AC/CB state → alpha-vane ice-state response.
relationships: Ice accretion/removal rates are trainer values; the model is not a calibrated AOA sensor or stall-warning computer.
controls: LEFT ALPHA VANE HEAT / P6 CB

name: Right Alpha-Vane Heater / Ice State
function: Models the right alpha-vane heater power path and qualitative ice accretion/removal state under shared icing conditions.
flow: Icing condition + heater command + AC/CB state → alpha-vane ice-state response.
relationships: Ice accretion/removal rates are trainer values; the model is not a calibrated AOA sensor or stall-warning computer.
controls: RIGHT ALPHA VANE HEAT / P6 CB

name: Interactive P6 Circuit-Breaker Trainer Subset
function: Provides interactive open/reset behavior for explicitly modeled breaker paths and links those paths to shared simulator state.
flow: User CB pull/reset → shared breaker state → gated system controls, loads and indications.
relationships: Not a complete serial/effectivity-specific P6 reproduction; exact breaker names, bus assignments and wire/pin mappings require the applicable WDM diagram sheets.
